Definition: from G2632; an adverse sentence (the verdict):--condemnation.
BiblicalUsage: Condemnation is the sentence hanging over us, and Paul sets it against the free gift: the judgment was by one offence to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. By one man's offence judgment came upon all men, and by one man's obedience the free gift came upon all men. Then comes the word that undoes it all: there is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there is no condemnation for me because the sentence fell on Christ instead. I hold that this is the whole gospel in one verse, and I will stand on it when the accuser comes.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
